receipt.public_excerpt: the IC3 report features a section on artificial intelligence, which accounts for 22,364 complaints, costing Americans nearly $893 million.

evidence_items.explanation: Official US figures for 2025 show more than 22,000 AI-related cybercrime complaints and about $893 million in losses. This meets the large-scale threshold in the early resolution rule.

receipt.public_excerpt: We recently disrupted a sophisticated cybercriminal that used Claude Code to commit large-scale theft and extortion of personal data. The actor targeted at least 17 distinct organizations

evidence_items.explanation: An AI developer confirms a large criminal extortion operation run with a generative AI coding agent in 2025. The same report also describes AI-built ransomware sold to other criminals.

receipt.public_excerpt: AI has lowered the barriers to sophisticated cybercrime. Criminals with few technical skills are using AI to conduct complex operations, such as developing ransomware

evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic's own finding is that generative AI is widening who can commit sophisticated cybercrime. This fits the forecast of a lot of GenAI-driven cybercrime.

unresolved_gaps: AI-related complaints were about 2% of the 1,008,597 total IC3 complaints in 2025 (22,364 / 1,008,597). Whether that counts as 'a lot' depends on reading the claim in absolute rather than relative terms.
The FBI counts a complaint as AI-related only when the victim mentions AI, so the true scale is uncertain in both directions.
